prefixes.title: Native API
prefixes.summary: User-visible Native API syscall entrypoint, typically reached from user mode through ntdll and serviced in the kernel.
notes: Often paired with a matching Zw* form in kernel code.
Common in ntdll.dll and ntoskrnl.exe exports.

prefixes.title: Zw Native API
prefixes.summary: Kernel-mode form of a Native API service. Zw* names usually map to the same service family as Nt* with call-context differences.
notes: Usually used by kernel-mode callers.
Probe and previous-mode behavior can differ from the Nt* path.

prefixes.title: Process Manager
prefixes.summary: Process manager routines for processes, threads, jobs, silos, and related executive objects.
notes: Often deals with EPROCESS, ETHREAD, tokens, and silo state.

prefixes.title: Process Manager Private
prefixes.summary: Private process manager helper used inside the kernel implementation rather than as a public executive entrypoint.
notes: Usually implementation detail behind Ps* services.

prefixes.title: Executive Support
prefixes.summary: Executive support routines for handles, pools, rundown protection, push locks, resources, and general kernel services.
notes: Common in handle-table, locking, and pool-management code.

prefixes.title: Kernel Executive
prefixes.summary: Core kernel primitive routines for IRQL, synchronization, scheduling, APCs, timers, and processor state.
notes: Generally stable kernel building blocks used by higher layers.

prefixes.title: Kernel Internal
prefixes.summary: Private kernel internals, commonly tied to traps, dispatch, APC delivery, interrupt paths, or scheduler implementation details.
notes: Usually lower-level and less stable than Ke* entrypoints.

prefixes.title: Security Reference Monitor
prefixes.summary: Security subsystem routines for subject context capture, access checks, auditing, descriptors, and token-related work.
notes: Often appears around access checks and privilege evaluation.

prefixes.title: Security Private
prefixes.summary: Private security subsystem helpers behind Se* entrypoints, frequently involved in auditing, privilege checks, and access-state plumbing.
notes: Usually internal implementation detail rather than a public executive surface.

prefixes.title: Object Manager
prefixes.summary: Object manager routines for object lookup, naming, handle creation, referencing, and lifetime management.
notes: Common around handles, reference counts, and object namespace operations.

prefixes.title: Object Manager Private
prefixes.summary: Private object manager helper used internally for handle tracing, reference bookkeeping, and namespace implementation details.
notes: Usually backs higher-level Ob* operations.

prefixes.title: Runtime Library
prefixes.summary: Runtime support routines for strings, memory, SIDs, exceptions, lists, and general helper logic used across user and kernel mode.
notes: Many Rtl* helpers exist in both ntdll and ntoskrnl contexts.

prefixes.title: File System Runtime Library
prefixes.summary: Filesystem runtime helpers used by file systems and filter drivers for name handling, oplocks, notifications, and common FS support code.
notes: Longer prefix than Rtl; should win during prefix matching.

prefixes.title: Memory Manager
prefixes.summary: Memory manager routines for virtual memory, sections, paging, faults, MDLs, and address-space operations.
notes: Common around section mapping, protection changes, and fault handling.

prefixes.title: I/O Manager
prefixes.summary: I/O manager routines for IRPs, device objects, file objects, driver dispatch, and request routing.
notes: Frequently used by drivers and filesystem code.

prefixes.title: Configuration Manager
prefixes.summary: Registry and configuration manager routines for hive, key, and value operations.
notes: Registry-oriented kernel subsystem.

prefixes.title: Configuration Manager Private
prefixes.summary: Private configuration manager internals used behind Cm* registry operations.
notes: Usually implementation detail for registry code paths.

prefixes.title: Hardware Abstraction Layer
prefixes.summary: HAL routines abstract interrupt controllers, timers, processors, buses, and other platform-specific hardware behavior.
notes: Often platform and chipset sensitive.

prefixes.title: Event Tracing for Windows
prefixes.summary: ETW tracing routines for logging structured events, telemetry, and provider activity.
notes: Common around audit, diagnostics, and telemetry paths.

prefixes.title: Cache Manager
prefixes.summary: Cache manager routines for file caching, lazy writing, read-ahead, and cache coherency support.
notes: Frequently used by filesystem drivers.

prefixes.title: Power Manager
prefixes.summary: Power manager routines for sleep states, device power transitions, and system power policy.
notes: Appears in platform power policy and device state handling.

prefixes.title: Executive Private
prefixes.summary: Private executive support helpers that implement the internal mechanisms behind public Ex* services, including handle tables, callback objects, system information dispatch, resource management, and pool bookkeeping.
notes: Implementation-layer counterpart to Ex*; not directly callable from drivers.
Commonly encountered in handle-table walk, callback-object, and system-info paths.
Longer prefix than Ex and must win prefix matching against it.

prefixes.title: Loader
prefixes.summary: PE image loader routines for DLL loading, image mapping, relocations, imports, and TLS initialization in both user and kernel mode.
notes: User-mode Ldr* lives in ntdll; kernel-mode variants appear in ntoskrnl.
Common in injection, shellcode, and DLL-hijacking analysis.

prefixes.title: Windows Management Instrumentation
prefixes.summary: WMI and kernel-tracing routines for provider registration, data-block dispatch, and event notification.
notes: Overlaps with ETW paths in modern builds.

prefixes.title: Debug Support
prefixes.summary: Kernel debug-support routines for breakpoint management, debug-port I/O, and debugger communication.
notes: Appears in kernel debugger attach and breakpoint paths.

prefixes.title: Driver Verifier
prefixes.summary: Driver Verifier routines that instrument pool, IRP, and lock operations to catch driver bugs at runtime.
notes: Only active when verifier is enabled; presence indicates instrumented code paths.

verbs.summary: Retrieve information without directly modifying the target state.
Modify an existing setting, property, or state value.
Open an existing object and usually return a handle.
Create a new object or system resource.
Close a handle or terminate access to an object.
Read data from the target object or address range.
Write data into the target object or address range.
Map one object or range into an address space or view.
Remove a previous mapping from an address space or view.
Reserve or commit resources such as memory.
Release previously allocated resources.
Change protection attributes such as memory access permissions.
Acquire or increment a reference to an object.
Release or decrement a reference to an object.
Snapshot or copy caller-supplied state into a trusted kernel-owned form.
Release previously captured or acquired context/state.
Delete or tear down an existing object or state block.
Search for and resolve a target object or entry.
Raise an exception, status, or execution level.
Test a condition or validate a state.
Flush buffered or cached state.
Duplicate an existing object, handle, or reference.

objects.summary: System-wide information classes and kernel or OS state.
Process information classes or process properties.
Thread information classes or thread properties.
Virtual memory regions and address-space state.
A mapped view of a section object in an address space.
objects.phrase: a section view into an address space

objects.summary: A section object, typically used for mapped files or shared memory.
A process object.
A thread object.
A file object or filesystem target.
A generic executive object or object-manager managed target.
A handle table entry or object handle.
A security token representing identity and privileges.
A security identifier.
Captured access-check state used during security evaluation.
Captured subject context for security checks and auditing.
Privilege state or privilege-check information.
Kernel pool memory.
A push lock synchronization primitive.
An address or address-based wait target.
Kernel APC delivery state.
A datatype misalignment exception condition.

exact_symbols.summary: Queries a selected system-information class from the Native API layer.
notes: The exact data returned depends on the SYSTEM_INFORMATION_CLASS value.
Frequently used by diagnostics, enumeration, and security tooling.

exact_symbols.summary: Opens a process object and returns a handle after validating access.
notes: Typically feeds object-manager and security checks before handle creation.

exact_symbols.summary: Opens a thread object and returns a handle after validating access.
notes: Often parallels NtOpenProcess but targets ETHREAD-backed objects.

exact_symbols.summary: Queries one of several process information classes for a target process.
notes: The meaning of the buffer depends on PROCESSINFOCLASS.

exact_symbols.summary: Queries one of several thread information classes for a target thread.
notes: The meaning of the buffer depends on THREADINFOCLASS.

exact_symbols.summary: Allocates or reserves virtual memory in a process address space.
notes: Common in loaders, allocators, and code-injection workflows.

exact_symbols.summary: Releases or decommits virtual memory in a process address space.
notes: Pairs naturally with NtAllocateVirtualMemory.

exact_symbols.summary: Changes access protections on a virtual memory region.
notes: Common in JIT, loader, and memory-permission transitions.

exact_symbols.summary: Reads memory from a target process address space.
notes: Common in debuggers, diagnostics, and memory-inspection tools.

exact_symbols.summary: Writes memory into a target process address space.
notes: Common in debuggers, injectors, and patching workflows.

exact_symbols.summary: Creates or opens a file object through the Native API path.
notes: The create disposition and options determine whether this behaves like open, create, overwrite, or supersede.

exact_symbols.summary: Creates a section object for mapped files, images, or shared memory.
notes: Section objects are commonly consumed by mapping and image-loading paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Maps a section view into a process address space.
notes: Common in image loading, shared memory, and injection chains.

exact_symbols.summary: Removes a previously mapped section view from a process address space.
notes: Often paired with NtMapViewOfSection.

exact_symbols.summary: Duplicates a handle or object reference into a target process handle table.
notes: Used for handle transfer and brokered access patterns.

exact_symbols.summary: Closes a handle and releases the associated handle-table reference.
notes: Simple surface, but the object-manager cleanup it triggers can be deeper.

exact_symbols.summary: Internal process-manager helper that performs the kernel-side work behind opening a process object.
notes: Often appears under NtOpenProcess in ntoskrnl call maps.

exact_symbols.summary: References a process primary token with tagged object-reference bookkeeping.
notes: Useful when tracking token access and object lifetime.

exact_symbols.summary: Internal kernel routine that checks whether pending kernel APC delivery should occur.
notes: Sits in low-level scheduler and APC state transitions.

exact_symbols.summary: Private security helper that evaluates requested privileges against the current security context.
notes: Common during object-open and access-validation paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Captures the current subject security context for later access checks or auditing.
notes: Usually paired with SeReleaseSubjectContext.

exact_symbols.summary: Releases a previously captured subject context.
notes: Cleanup companion to SeCaptureSubjectContext.

exact_symbols.summary: Compares two security identifiers to determine whether they represent the same SID.
notes: Common in security and token code paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Private executive helper that performs the real work behind NtQuerySystemInformation after the dispatch table routes to the correct handler.
notes: Called from NtQuerySystemInformation's indirect dispatch; handles the actual buffer fill for the given SYSTEM_INFORMATION_CLASS.
Most system-info classes ultimately end up here before delegating to subsystem-specific helpers.

exact_symbols.summary: Creates a callback object used by the executive callback notification mechanism.
notes: Backs ExCreateCallback; callback objects are used by PsSet* and other notify-routine registrations.
The callback object stores a list of registered routines invoked by ExpNotifyCallback.

exact_symbols.summary: Tears down a callback object and releases its associated resources.
notes: Called when the last reference to a callback object is released.

exact_symbols.summary: Fires all routines registered against a callback object in sequence.
notes: Backs ExNotifyCallback; iterates the callback object's registration list.
Common in driver notification, power, and configuration-change paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Registers a routine with an existing callback object.
notes: Backs ExRegisterCallback; adds a CALLBACK_REGISTRATION to the object's list.

exact_symbols.summary: Removes a previously registered routine from a callback object.
notes: Backs ExUnregisterCallback; must be balanced with ExpRegisterCallback.

exact_symbols.summary: Looks up a handle-table entry by handle value in the executive handle table.
notes: Core of the handle-table B-tree walk; called from ObpReferenceObjectByHandle and related paths.
Returns a locked EXHANDLE_TABLE_ENTRY pointer; caller must release the lock.

exact_symbols.summary: Allocates a new executive handle table, optionally inheriting entries from a parent.
notes: Called at process/session creation or when the handle table must be expanded.
The resulting table is managed by the object manager via Ob* routines.

exact_symbols.summary: Releases all storage belonging to an executive handle table.
notes: Called on process teardown after all handles have been closed.
Walks the table structure and frees each page of handle entries.

exact_symbols.summary: Finds a handle table entry by scanning the table for a matching object pointer.
notes: Reverse-direction lookup compared to ExpLookupHandleTableEntry.
Less common; appears in auditing and handle-trace code paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Callback invoked per handle entry during a handle-table duplication walk.
notes: Used by NtDuplicateObject and process-fork paths to propagate inheritable handles.

exact_symbols.summary: Walks a handle table and closes all remaining handles during process rundown.
notes: Called late in process teardown to ensure no leaked handles remain.
Triggers object-manager cleanup for each still-open handle.

exact_symbols.summary: Retrieves system control values from the registry for kernel-mode configuration.
notes: Reads NLS, memory, and subsystem tuning parameters during initialization.
Called from system-information paths and early boot configuration.

exact_symbols.summary: Deletes a kernel performance-profiling object.
notes: Backs NtStopProfile / profile object lifecycle; releases profiling buffers and timers.

exact_symbols.summary: Blocks the calling thread until a ERESOURCE exclusive or shared acquisition succeeds.
notes: Slow path of ExAcquireResourceExclusiveLite / ExAcquireResourceSharedLite.
Puts the caller into a wait state; appears in heavily-contended resource code paths.

exact_symbols.summary: Entry point for executive worker threads that process items queued to the ExWorkerQueue.
notes: Worker threads call this loop to dequeue and execute WORK_QUEUE_ITEM callbacks.
Critical path for asynchronous kernel operations; stalls here indicate queue backup.

exact_symbols.summary: Inserts a WORK_QUEUE_ITEM onto the appropriate executive worker queue.
notes: Backs ExQueueWorkItem; selects the CriticalWorkQueue, DelayedWorkQueue, or HyperCriticalWorkQueue.

exact_symbols.summary: Sets the system timer resolution to the requested 100-ns tick interval.
notes: Backs NtSetTimerResolution; affects the global timer tick period.
Resolution changes are reference-counted across callers.

exact_symbols.summary: Priority-boosts the thread that owns a resource or push lock to reduce contention.
notes: Called when a waiter is blocked on a resource held by a lower-priority thread.
Part of the priority-inheritance mechanism in resource/push-lock paths.
